page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the in-house Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 ARM64 processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 4 physical cores at a 2.75 GHz clock speed, omitting simultaneous multithreading for predictable execution. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 64 MB of L3 cache, alongside native hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes, and offers a baseline network speed of 3 Gbps.

Performance assessments reflect moderate throughput across general compute and memory-centric workloads. In stress-ng testing, the instance registers 1818.58 points in single-core and 7235.59 points in multi-core routines. The memory interface delivers 408.75 GB/s in small-block cached read operations and 74.83 GB/s for large uncached blocks. Application-layer benchmarks demonstrate solid utility, reaching 6.89 million operations per second on Redis SET commands and 6.85 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Compression tasks scale effectively, with bzip3 reaching 45.16 GB/s across multiple threads. However, PassMark tests indicate lower efficiency in complex extended instruction and encryption routines, and machine learning text generation degrades significantly on models larger than lightweight parameter sets.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated non-hyperthreaded ARM64 cores deliver stable execution without neighbor-thread contention, providing consistent performance per core. The absence of integrated NVMe storage and the 3 Gbps network limit mean high-throughput database clusters may experience I/O bottlenecks. Consequently, the ecs.c8y.xlarge is well fitted for stateless web serving, ARM64 containerized microservices, build and CI/CD pipelines, and lightweight caching tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the proprietary Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 ARM64 processor running at 2.75 GHz. Built on a KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. It provides 8.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU, alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data. In empirical benchmarks, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-core stress performance, 6.89 million Redis SET operations per second, and 6.85 GB/s in static web serving throughput. However, synthetic testing highlights lower capabilities in cryptographic execution and heavier machine learning generation. The ecs.c8y.xlarge offers an efficient architecture for mid-tier web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and lightweight in-memory caching where ARM-compatible codebases benefit from dedicated execution threads.
